<header>IV. 3. 5. UPARIPAÑCA CHAPTER 3. 127</header>

19. Then Ragā, the daughter of Māra, spoke this verse in the presence of the Blessed One:
"Having cut off craving, the leader of a company and community <note>original: "gaṇa-saṅgha-vârî"; usually read gaṇasaṅghacārī, "one who moves at the head of a group and an order"</note>,
surely many beings too will follow his course¹ <note>the manuscripts marked SS. read "will cross over"</note>.
Alas, this homeless one <note>original: "anoko", "one without a house", that is, the Buddha</note> will snatch away
many people and lead them to the far shore, beyond the King of Death."
20. "The great heroes, the <term>Tathāgatas</term> <gloss>Thus-gone Ones, a title of the Buddhas</gloss>, lead indeed by the true Dhamma.
When those who understand are led by the Dhamma, what room is there for envy?"
21. Then Taṇhā, Arati and Ragā, the daughters of Māra, went to where Māra the Evil One was.
22. Māra the Evil One saw Taṇhā, Arati and Ragā, his daughters, coming from afar. Seeing them, he addressed them in verses:
"Fools! You tried to crush a mountain with lotus stalks,
to dig up a hill with your fingernails, to chew iron with your teeth.
As though you had lifted a rock upon your heads, you sought a footing in the bottomless abyss;
as though you had struck your breast against a stump, you come away from Gotama disheartened."
23. Glittering they had come, Taṇhā, Arati and Ragā;
the Teacher swept them away right there, as the wind sweeps off a fallen tuft of cotton.
<note>Taṇhā, Arati and Ragā are personifications: "Craving", "Discontent" and "Lust". Their failed attempt to seduce the Buddha closes the collection of discourses on Māra.</note>

->The Third Chapter.<-
->Its summary verse:<-
The Many, and Samiddhi, Godhika, the Seven Years,
the Daughters: this pentad on Māra was taught by the Buddha, the Teacher. The Connected Discourses on Māra are complete.
<note>The summary verse <term>uddāna</term> <gloss>mnemonic list of the discourses in a chapter</gloss> names the five suttas of this chapter by key words.</note>

---

¹ SS. read tarissanti <gloss>will cross over</gloss>. ² SS. read saddhā <gloss>faithful</gloss>. ³ B. reads aneko <gloss>not one, many</gloss>. ⁴ C. reads accheja. ⁵ S¹ niyya; S² nîyya°; B. and C. nayya°; S¹ nîyyamânam. ⁶ B. reads usuyâ. ⁷ SS. read gâtham. ⁸ S¹ reads khâṇam. ⁹ SS. read Gotamanti. ¹⁰ So the SS.; B. daddalhamânâ; C. daddalhamânâ. ¹¹ SS. read Taṇhâ ca. ¹² SS. omit ca. ¹³ S¹ tûlabhaṭṭham; S².³ tula-haṭṭham. ¹⁴ SS. read mâruto; B. mâluto. ¹⁵ B. reads catuttho <gloss>fourth</gloss>. ¹⁶ SS. have "uparipañca" instead of "tatiyo" (or "catuttho") vaggo. ¹⁷ B. reads Tatruddânam bhavati <gloss>Here is the summary</gloss>.

<summary>This page closes the Māra Saṃyutta with the end of the story of Māra's three daughters, Craving, Discontent and Lust, who fail to tempt the Buddha and are mocked by their father in verse. It ends with the chapter's mnemonic summary verse and Feer's textual variants.</summary>
